newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka charter to stress children's rights.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka charter to stress children's rights.

text.p: Sri Lanka's new constitution will stress children's rights and contain "enforceable" safeguards against drug pushing, paedophilia, and forced labour of minors, the government said on Saturday.
"In its proposals the Government has focused special attention on children's rights," the People's Alliance (PA) administration of President Chandrika Kumaratunga said.

"Among the new rights proposed are the right to a name from birth, protection from maltreatment, neglect, abuse, degradation and exploitative labour practices, protection from exposure to physical and moral hazards," a government statement said.
In recent years, Sri Lanka's beaches and resorts have become notorious for paedophile activities and child trafficking.
The government said the draft constitution will incorporate a special article for children's rights, and also cover minors through separate provisions against slavery and forced labour.
The draft constitution, which primarily aims to devolve power to minorities and end the country's 13-year-old ethnic crisis, is currently being debated by a parliamentary select committee.
But discussions have stalled due to differences between Sri Lanka's various political parties.
The government has said it plans to bring the constitutional reform proposals to parliament before the budget session in November.
